scope: Read-only review of existing results; no rerun or result changes
video_generation: Nine source objects sequentially repeated, sizes preserved
interpretation: Long interruption in application scheduling and completed reception precedes video queue evictions. Exact transport cause requires socket/buffer/recovery telemetry; cache size and priority alone are insufficient explanations.
audit_gap: Current transport-stall audit checks only unfinished in_service/in_transport rows at cutoff. File 535 eventually delivered and escaped the audit despite 2686.803 s transport time.
additional_config_mismatch: Integration Score uses stream array index for Zipf weights; current phase-three report specifies separate rank D3,D4,D1,D2,I1,V1.
conclusion: Do not treat current WO_COMPRESSION video loss as validated evidence of algorithm effect until transport interruption and configuration consistency are resolved.

additional_confirmed_source_bug.issue: C++ ^ is bitwise XOR, not exponentiation. Observed multipliers for retry counts 0..7 are 2,3,0,1,6,7,4,5; this is not exponential backoff and count 2 gives a zero multiplier before the minimum is re-applied on the next alarm calculation.
additional_confirmed_source_bug.impact: This can distort QUIC loss-recovery timing under the 2.5–16.4% packet-loss segment present during the file stall. It is a plausible direct transport cause, but current traces do not include per-RTO counters/timestamps to prove it caused this specific 2687 s stall.
additional_confirmed_source_bug.scope: The defect applies to QUIC retransmission alarm timing wherever the patched simulator is used.

wire_activity_caveat: Dispatch/complete-file traces prove no subsequent application file was dispatched and no complete file was received during the interval. They do not prove zero QUIC packets on the wire: the already-started stream may have emitted retransmissions, ACKs, or probes. Per-interval packet capture/counters were not recorded.
follow_up: Fix the QUIC RTO multiplier with capped exponential backoff; add RTO/alarm, cwnd/bytes-in-flight, retransmitted-byte and per-interval packet telemetry; rerun affected ablations before interpreting protocol/compression comparisons.
